content:
The image shows soybean plants with bright green, moist stems alongside fully matured, tan/brown dried pods. The stark contrast — green stems persisting while pods have completed maturation — is the hallmark of Green Stem Disorder.

Key visual evidence:
- Stems are vivid green and clearly still turgid/moist
- Pods are fully mature (tan/brown, dried out)
- No lesions, fungal growth, pustules, or necrosis visible
- Pattern matches exactly: "stems stay moist and green while pods mature normally"

No other disease fits this pattern. Bacterial blight, rust, and other foliar diseases would show leaf lesions. BSR and SDS would show internal stem browning and leaf symptoms. This is purely a green stem/pod maturity mismatch.
